components.name: unamentis
components.description: Top-level UnaMentis monorepo containing the iOS app, watchOS companion, server infrastructure, web clients, curriculum content, and documentation.

children.name: WatchModels
children.description: Shared data models used by both the iOS app and watchOS companion for inter-device communication.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shared Swift models that define the data contract between the iOS app and Apple Watch companion. These models are used for WatchConnectivity transfers, ensuring both platforms serialize and deserialize session data identically.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Shared session state, Knowledge Bowl scores, and connectivity payloads between iOS and watchOS

children.name: TestResults.xcresult
children.description: Xcode test result bundle containing test execution logs and coverage data.

ai_enhance.help_text: This is an Xcode test results bundle (.xcresult) generated by running the test suite. It contains test pass/fail data, code coverage reports, and performance metrics. It is a build artifact, not source code.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Test execution results, code coverage metrics, and performance baselines

children.name: UnaMentis
children.description: The main UnaMentis iOS application, an AI-powered educational platform featuring conversational tutoring, Knowledge Bowl quiz training, curriculum management, and reading comprehension tools.

children.name: Tab Bar
children.description: 5 tabs

children.name: Learning
children.description: Entry: Learning

children.name: Modules
children.description: Grid view displaying available learning modules with progress indicators and topic counts.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays all available curriculum modules in a grid layout. Each module shows its title, topic count, and the user's completion progress. Tapping a module navigates to the curriculum detail view. This is the entry point for curriculum-based learning.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Module metadata, completion percentages, topic counts

children.name: Curriculum Detail
children.description: Detail view for a curriculum module showing its topics, descriptions, and learning progress.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows detailed information about a selected curriculum module including its topics, descriptions, and per-topic progress. Users can select topics to drill into or start study sessions. Presented as a sheet from the curriculum list.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Module details, topic list, progress per topic, session launch parameters

children.name: KBDashboard
children.description: Knowledge Bowl dashboard showing training modes, domain mastery progress, and quick-start options for competitive quiz practice.

ai_enhance.help_text: The central hub for Knowledge Bowl training. Displays available practice modes (written, oral, match simulation, conference, rebound, domain drill), domain mastery progress bars, and quick-start configuration. Navigates to specific training sessions and presents settings as sheets. This is the most complex screen in the app.
ai_enhance.data_handled: KB training mode selection, domain mastery scores, quick-start preferences, session configuration

children.name: Topic Detail
children.description: Detailed view of a curriculum topic showing questions, study materials, and the option to start a tutoring session.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows detailed information for a specific curriculum topic including its questions and study materials. Users can launch a full-screen tutoring session from here. Presented as a sheet from the curriculum detail view.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Topic content, associated questions, session launch configuration

children.name: KBWritten Session
children.description: Written Knowledge Bowl practice session where users answer questions by typing, with scoring and time tracking.

ai_enhance.help_text: Simulates the written round of a Knowledge Bowl competition. Users type answers to questions within time limits. Tracks scoring using competition rules and provides immediate feedback on correctness. Depends on the KB question bank and scoring algorithms.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Questions, typed answers, scoring state, timer, session results

children.name: KBOral Session
children.description: Oral Knowledge Bowl practice session using speech recognition for answer input with real-time scoring.

ai_enhance.help_text: Simulates the oral round of Knowledge Bowl where users speak their answers. Uses the STT service for speech recognition and scores responses using competition rules. Provides real-time feedback and tracks buzzer timing. Depends on audio services and the KB scoring engine.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Audio input, speech-to-text results, oral answers, scoring, buzzer timing

children.name: KBMatch Simulation
children.description: Full match simulation recreating a competitive Knowledge Bowl match with multiple rounds and AI opponents.

ai_enhance.help_text: Provides a full competitive simulation of a Knowledge Bowl match, including written and oral rounds with simulated AI opponents. Uses the team management and match algorithms to create realistic competition scenarios. This is the most immersive training mode.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Match state, round progression, team scores, AI opponent actions, question sequences

children.name: KBConference Training
children.description: Conference-style training mode where users practice collaborative team discussion and answer strategies.

ai_enhance.help_text: Trains users in the conference segment of Knowledge Bowl, where team members discuss and agree on answers before buzzing. Simulates team dynamics and collaborative answer strategies. Uses KB algorithms for scoring and question selection.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Conference round questions, team discussion simulation, collaborative answers, scoring

children.name: KBRebound Training
children.description: Rebound training mode practicing the strategy of answering after another team's incorrect response.

ai_enhance.help_text: Trains the rebound strategy in Knowledge Bowl where users practice answering questions after a simulated opponent gives an incorrect answer. Builds quick-thinking skills and secondary knowledge recall. Uses KB algorithms for opponent simulation.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Rebound scenarios, opponent incorrect answers, user responses, timing, scoring

children.name: KBDomain Drill
children.description: Focused practice on a specific knowledge domain with targeted question sets for mastery improvement.

ai_enhance.help_text: Allows focused practice on a single knowledge domain (e.g., Science, History, Literature). Presents questions filtered by domain with difficulty progression based on the user's mastery level. Uses spaced repetition principles to target weak areas.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Domain-filtered questions, mastery scores, difficulty progression, drill results

children.name: KBSettings
children.description: Knowledge Bowl settings for configuring training preferences, difficulty levels, and domain weights.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configuration screen for Knowledge Bowl training parameters. Users can adjust difficulty levels, set domain weights for question selection, configure timing rules, and customize training session preferences. Presented as a sheet from the KB dashboard.
ai_enhance.data_handled: KB configuration: difficulty, domain weights, timing rules, session preferences

children.name: KBQuickstart Settings
children.description: Quick-start configuration for rapidly launching a Knowledge Bowl practice session with preset parameters.

ai_enhance.help_text: Streamlined configuration for quickly launching a KB practice session. Users select a training mode, domain mix, and duration without going through full settings. Presents domain mix configuration as a sheet. Designed for rapid session start.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Quick-start presets, selected mode, domain mix, session duration

children.name: KBGetting Started Help
children.description: Getting started guide for Knowledge Bowl training features and terminology.

ai_enhance.help_text: Help screen explaining Knowledge Bowl basics: what it is, how training modes work, and how to get started. Provides context for new users unfamiliar with academic quiz competitions. This is a read-only help screen accessible from the KB dashboard.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content and documentation text

children.name: KBTraining Modes Help
children.description: Help documentation explaining each Knowledge Bowl training mode and when to use it.

ai_enhance.help_text: Describes each KB training mode (written, oral, match simulation, conference, rebound, domain drill) with tips on when to use each. Helps users choose the right practice approach. This is a read-only help screen accessible from the KB dashboard.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content and documentation text

children.name: KBStrategy Help
children.description: Strategy guide for competitive Knowledge Bowl with tips on buzzer timing and team coordination.

ai_enhance.help_text: Provides competitive strategy advice for Knowledge Bowl including buzzer timing, question anticipation, team communication, and domain specialization tips. This is a read-only help screen accessible from the KB dashboard.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content and documentation text

children.name: KBRegional Rules Help
children.description: Reference for Knowledge Bowl regional rule variations across different competition circuits.

ai_enhance.help_text: Documents rule variations across different Knowledge Bowl regional circuits. Covers scoring differences, round formats, and competition-specific regulations. This is a read-only help screen accessible from the KB dashboard.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content and documentation text

children.name: KBDomain Mix
children.description: Configuration view for adjusting the proportion of questions from each knowledge domain in practice sessions.

ai_enhance.help_text: Allows users to configure the mix of knowledge domains (Science, History, Math, Literature, etc.) used in KB practice sessions. Users can weight domains to focus on weak areas or create balanced practice sets. Presented as a sheet from quick-start settings.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Domain weight percentages, domain list, mix presets

children.name: KBCreate Pack
children.description: Interface for creating custom question packs from available curriculum content for targeted practice.

ai_enhance.help_text: Allows users to create custom question packs by selecting questions from the curriculum database. Users can filter by domain, difficulty, and topic to build targeted practice sets. Created packs integrate with all KB training modes.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Question selection, pack metadata, domain and difficulty filters

children.name: Curriculum Download Flow
children.description: Multi-step flow for downloading curriculum content from the server, with progress tracking and error handling.

ai_enhance.help_text: Manages the multi-step process of downloading curriculum modules from the management server. Shows download progress, handles network errors with retry logic, and validates downloaded content. Depends on the curriculum service and server API.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Download progress, curriculum package data, network status, validation results

children.name: Curriculum
children.description: Main curriculum browsing view listing available modules with search and filtering capabilities.

ai_enhance.help_text: The primary curriculum browsing screen showing all available learning modules. Supports search, filtering by domain, and displays download status for server-hosted content. Tapping a module presents its detail view as a sheet.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Curriculum module list, search queries, filter state, download status

children.name: KBDomain Mastery
children.description: Visualization of mastery progress across all Knowledge Bowl domains with historical trend data.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays the user's mastery level across all KB domains using progress bars and trend charts. Shows historical performance data to track improvement over time. Uses the KB scoring algorithms to compute mastery metrics.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Domain mastery scores, historical trends, performance metrics

children.name: KBEnhanced Validation Setup
children.description: Setup screen for enhanced validation mode that uses ML-based answer scoring with configurable thresholds.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configures enhanced validation settings that use ML models to score free-form answers beyond simple string matching. Users can adjust scoring thresholds, enable/disable ML validation, and test the system. Depends on the KB ML service.
ai_enhance.data_handled: ML validation thresholds, scoring configuration, test inputs and results

children.name: Kyutai Pocket Settings
children.description: Settings for the Kyutai Pocket on-device speech model including voice selection and audio recording configuration.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configuration screen for the Kyutai Pocket on-device speech model. Users can select voice profiles, adjust audio recording parameters, and test the model. Presents the audio recorder as a sheet for voice testing. Part of the on-device ML stack.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Kyutai model settings, voice profiles, audio recording configuration

children.name: Server Curriculum Detail
children.description: Detail view for server-hosted curriculum showing content preview and download options.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows details of curriculum content hosted on the management server. Users can preview module content, see topic breakdowns, and initiate downloads. Differs from the local curriculum detail view by pulling data from the server API.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Server curriculum metadata, content previews, download triggers

children.name: Topic Selection
children.description: Topic picker allowing users to select specific topics within a curriculum module for focused study.

ai_enhance.help_text: Presents a selectable list of topics within a curriculum module. Users can pick one or multiple topics to study in a focused session. Supports filtering and shows completion status per topic.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Topic list, selection state, completion indicators

ai_enhance.help_text: The Learning tab contains curriculum browsing, Knowledge Bowl dashboard, and all KB training modes. It is the most feature-rich tab, housing the core educational content and competitive quiz functionality. Users spend the majority of their time here.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Curriculum modules, KB session state, training mode selection, domain mastery progress

children.name: Chat
children.description: Entry: Session Tab Content

children.name: Session
children.description: Main conversational tutoring session view with real-time AI chat, voice input, and TTS playback.

ai_enhance.help_text: The primary tutoring session interface where users interact with an AI tutor. Supports text and voice input, displays conversation messages in a chat format, and plays TTS responses. Manages the full session lifecycle from start to end. Depends on LLM, STT, and TTS services.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Conversation messages, voice audio input/output, session state, LLM context, TTS audio playback

children.name: Voice Settings
children.description: Voice configuration screen for selecting TTS voices, STT engines, and audio playback preferences.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configures voice-related settings including TTS voice selection, STT engine choice, audio playback speed, and pitch adjustments. Navigates to the Chatterbox and TTS tuning sub-screens. Presented as a sheet from the session view.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Voice provider selection, TTS/STT configuration, audio playback parameters

children.name: Transcript
children.description: Read-only transcript of a completed tutoring session showing the full conversation with timestamps.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays the complete transcript of a tutoring session with timestamps and speaker labels. Allows users to review past conversations, copy text, and track session duration. Read-only view accessed from session history.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Session transcript messages, timestamps, speaker attribution

children.name: Chatterbox Settings
children.description: Advanced settings for the Chatterbox TTS engine including voice cloning and custom audio recording.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configuration for the Chatterbox TTS engine which supports voice cloning from recorded audio samples. Users can record voice samples via the audio recorder sheet, adjust synthesis parameters, and preview generated speech.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Chatterbox TTS config, voice clone samples, synthesis parameters

children.name: Audio Recorder
children.description: Audio recording interface for capturing voice samples used in TTS voice cloning.

ai_enhance.help_text: Simple audio recording screen for capturing voice samples. Used by the Chatterbox and Kyutai settings for voice cloning. Records audio, shows waveform visualization, and saves to the app's audio storage.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Audio recording buffers, waveform data, saved audio file references

ai_enhance.help_text: The Chat tab hosts AI-powered conversational tutoring sessions. Users can have free-form educational conversations with an LLM tutor, configure voice settings, and review session transcripts. Supports both text and voice input modes.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Conversation messages, voice audio streams, TTS playback, session transcripts

children.name: Assistant
children.description: Entry: Assistant Tab

children.name: Todo List
children.description: Main todo list showing learning tasks organized by status with swipe actions for completion and archiving.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays the user's learning-related todo items organized by status (active, completed, archived). Supports swipe gestures for status changes, navigation to detail views, and presents item details as sheets.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Reading List
children.description: Reading list showing saved articles and documents with progress tracking and categorization.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows saved reading materials organized by category. Tracks reading progress and supports adding new items via URL or manual entry. Users can open items in the reading reader view.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Reading data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Review List
children.description: Spaced repetition review list showing items due for review based on forgetting curve calculations.

ai_enhance.help_text: Lists items scheduled for spaced repetition review. Uses forgetting curve algorithms to determine review timing. Helps reinforce learning through systematic review of previously studied material.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Review data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Todo Item Detail
children.description: Detail view for a todo item showing notes, due dates, priority, and associated learning context.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows full details of a todo item including notes, due date, priority level, and any associated curriculum topic. Supports editing all fields. Presented as a sheet from the todo list.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Active Todo List
children.description: Filtered view showing only active (incomplete) todo items.

ai_enhance.help_text: Filtered subset of the todo list showing only active items. Provides a focused view for users who want to see only pending tasks without completed or archived items.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Completed Todo List
children.description: Filtered view showing completed todo items with completion dates.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows completed todo items with their completion timestamps. Users can archive or reactivate items from this view.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Archived Todo List
children.description: Filtered view showing archived todo items that can be restored if needed.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays archived todo items. Users can restore items to active status. Serves as a reference for past tasks.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Reading Reader
children.description: Full-screen reader for articles and documents with adjustable text size and reading progress tracking.

ai_enhance.help_text: Renders reading list content in a clean, distraction-free format. Supports adjustable text size, dark mode, and tracks reading position for progress. Depends on the reading list data model.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Reading data, user interactions, status changes

children.name: Reading Playback
children.description: Audio playback view for reading list items using TTS to read content aloud with speed controls.

ai_enhance.help_text: Plays back reading list content using TTS. Users can control playback speed, pause/resume, and follow along with highlighted text. Depends on the TTS service and reading playback service.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Reading data, user interactions, status changes

ai_enhance.help_text: The Assistant tab provides productivity tools: a todo list for tracking learning tasks, a reading list for managing articles and documents, and a review list for spaced repetition. These tools help users organize their study workflow.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Todo items with status tracking, reading list entries, review scheduling data

children.name: History
children.description: Entry: History

children.name: Session List
children.description: Chronological list of past tutoring and KB sessions with search and filtering by date and type.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays all past sessions in reverse chronological order. Users can search by content, filter by session type (tutoring vs KB), and navigate to detailed session views. Primary interface for session history.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Session list, search queries, filter state, session metadata

children.name: Session Detail
children.description: Detailed view of a past session showing transcript, scores, duration, and performance metrics.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows comprehensive details of a completed session including the full transcript, KB scores (if applicable), session duration, and token usage. Accessed by navigating from the session list.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Session details, transcript, scores, duration, cost/token metrics

ai_enhance.help_text: The History tab displays a chronological list of past tutoring and Knowledge Bowl sessions. Users can review session details including transcripts, scores, and performance metrics.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Session history records, timestamps, scores, and conversation logs

children.name: More
children.description: Entry: More Tab

children.name: TTSPlayback Tuning
children.description: Fine-tuning controls for TTS playback parameters including pitch, rate, and volume curves.

ai_enhance.help_text: Advanced controls for fine-tuning TTS playback parameters. Users can adjust pitch, speaking rate, volume curves, and pause duration. Changes are previewed in real-time.
ai_enhance.data_handled: TTS playback parameters: pitch, rate, volume, pause settings

children.name: Analytics
children.description: Analytics dashboard showing learning statistics, session counts, time spent, and progress trends.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays aggregated learning analytics including total sessions, time spent studying, KB accuracy trends, and curriculum completion rates. Uses charts and statistics to visualize progress.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Analytics data, session statistics, progress trends, chart data

children.name: Settings
children.description: Main settings screen providing access to all app configuration options organized by category.

ai_enhance.help_text: Central settings hub organizing configuration into categories: voice, LLM providers, server connection, diagnostics, and help. Navigates to specialized settings screens. Most configuration flows start here.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Settings navigation, configuration categories, app preferences

children.name: Quick Stats
children.description: Quick statistics summary showing key metrics like session count, accuracy, and streak data.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays a compact summary of key performance metrics. Shows session counts, average accuracy, current study streak, and domain coverage. Designed for at-a-glance progress review.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Summary statistics, session counts, accuracy averages, streak data

children.name: APIProvider Detail
children.description: Detail view for configuring an AI/LLM API provider with endpoint, key, and model selection.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configuration screen for a specific LLM API provider. Users enter API endpoint URL, API key, select models, and test the connection. Supports OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and custom providers.
ai_enhance.data_handled: API provider config: endpoint URL, API key, model list, connection test results

children.name: Session Cost Overview
children.description: Cost tracking view showing API token usage and estimated costs per session and cumulative.

ai_enhance.help_text: Displays token usage and estimated API costs broken down by session and cumulatively. Helps users monitor their LLM API spending. Shows input/output token counts and per-provider costs.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Token usage, cost estimates, per-session and cumulative spending

children.name: On Device LLMSettings
children.description: Settings for on-device LLM models including model selection, quantization, and memory limits.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configures on-device LLM inference using models like llama.cpp. Users select models, set quantization levels, configure memory limits, and manage model downloads. Part of the offline-capable stack.
ai_enhance.data_handled: On-device model selection, quantization settings, memory limits, download status

children.name: Server Settings
children.description: Server connection settings for the management server with URL, authentication, and sync configuration.

ai_enhance.help_text: Configures the connection to the UnaMentis management server. Users enter server URL, set up authentication, test connectivity, and configure data sync preferences. Can scan QR codes for quick setup.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Server URL, auth tokens, sync preferences, connection status

children.name: Diagnostics
children.description: System diagnostics showing device capabilities, service status, and debug information.

ai_enhance.help_text: Comprehensive diagnostics screen showing device hardware info, service health status, memory usage, and debug logs. Useful for troubleshooting issues with STT, TTS, or server connectivity.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Device info, service status, memory stats, debug logs

children.name: Device Metrics
children.description: Device performance metrics showing CPU, memory, and battery impact of app operations.

ai_enhance.help_text: Real-time device metrics display showing CPU usage, memory consumption, and battery drain during app operations. Helps identify performance bottlenecks in audio processing and ML inference.
ai_enhance.data_handled: CPU usage, memory stats, battery metrics, performance counters

children.name: Audio Test
children.description: Audio testing interface for verifying microphone input and speaker output with signal analysis.

ai_enhance.help_text: Tests audio hardware by recording from the microphone and playing through speakers. Shows signal waveforms, volume levels, and detects common audio issues. Used for troubleshooting voice features.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Audio test signals, microphone input levels, speaker output verification

children.name: Provider Test
children.description: API provider testing tool that sends test prompts and measures response latency and quality.

ai_enhance.help_text: Tests configured LLM providers by sending sample prompts and measuring response time, quality, and error rates. Helps users compare providers and verify their API configuration.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Test prompts, response latency, quality scores, error logs

children.name: Debug Conversation Test
children.description: Debug tool for testing conversation flows with raw LLM request/response inspection.

ai_enhance.help_text: Developer tool for debugging conversation flows. Shows raw LLM requests and responses, token counts, and conversation context. Useful for diagnosing issues with prompt engineering or context management.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Raw LLM messages, token counts, context window state, debug info

children.name: Help
children.description: Help hub providing access to feature guides, voice commands reference, and getting started documentation.

ai_enhance.help_text: Central help screen with navigation to feature-specific help pages. Covers free-form chat, curriculum, hands-free mode, voice commands, and settings. Entry point for all user documentation.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Help navigation, feature guide links

children.name: Voice Commands Help
children.description: Reference guide for available voice commands with examples and activation phrases.

ai_enhance.help_text: Lists all available voice commands with their trigger phrases and descriptions. Covers session control, navigation, and quiz-specific voice commands. Users can practice commands from this screen.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Voice command list, trigger phrases, descriptions

children.name: Onboarding
children.description: Initial onboarding flow for new users covering app features, permissions, and initial setup.

ai_enhance.help_text: Multi-step onboarding shown on first launch. Introduces app features, requests microphone permission, configures initial LLM provider, and sets up basic preferences. Presented as a full-screen modal from settings.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Onboarding steps, permission requests, initial configuration

children.name: Server Setup Guide
children.description: Step-by-step guide for setting up and connecting to the UnaMentis management server.

ai_enhance.help_text: Walks users through setting up a management server connection. Covers server installation, network configuration, and authentication. Includes QR code scanning for quick setup.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Setup instructions, server connection steps, QR code data

children.name: QRCode Scanner
children.description: Camera-based QR code scanner for quickly importing server connection configuration.

ai_enhance.help_text: Uses the device camera to scan QR codes containing server configuration. Automatically populates server URL and authentication settings. Presented as a sheet from server settings.
ai_enhance.data_handled: QR code data, camera feed, parsed server configuration

children.name: Freeform Chat Help
children.description: Help page explaining free-form chat features and conversation tips.

ai_enhance.help_text: Explains how to use the free-form chat tutoring mode, including conversation starters, topic switching, and how the AI tutor adapts to user level.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content about free-form chat features

children.name: Curriculum Help
children.description: Help page explaining curriculum features, module structure, and progress tracking.

ai_enhance.help_text: Documents the curriculum system: how modules are organized, how progress is tracked, how to download server content, and how curriculum connects to tutoring sessions.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content about curriculum features

children.name: Hands Free Help
children.description: Help page explaining hands-free voice mode for accessibility and multitasking.

ai_enhance.help_text: Explains the hands-free mode where users can interact with the app entirely through voice commands. Covers activation, available commands, and tips for best recognition accuracy.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content about hands-free mode

children.name: Settings Help
children.description: Help page explaining app settings categories and configuration options.

ai_enhance.help_text: Documents all settings categories and what each option controls. Helps users understand the impact of voice, LLM, server, and diagnostic settings.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Static help content about settings

children.name: Onboarding Page
children.description: Individual page within the onboarding flow displaying a single feature or setup step.

ai_enhance.help_text: Renders a single step in the onboarding flow. Each page covers one feature or setup task with illustrations and instructions. Part of the onboarding carousel.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Single onboarding step content, illustration, action button

ai_enhance.help_text: The More tab provides access to app settings, diagnostics, help documentation, analytics, and developer testing tools. It contains configuration for voice, LLM providers, server connections, and TTS playback tuning.
ai_enhance.data_handled: App configuration, diagnostic data, analytics summaries, API provider settings

ai_enhance.help_text: The main tab bar controller providing top-level navigation across five sections: Learning (curriculum and Knowledge Bowl), Chat (AI tutoring sessions), Assistant (todos, reading lists), History (past sessions), and More (settings, diagnostics). This is the primary navigation structure users interact with after onboarding.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Tab selection state and navigation stack for each tab

children.name: KBDomain Detail
children.description: Detailed view of a single knowledge domain showing mastery breakdown, question statistics, and practice history.

ai_enhance.help_text: Shows comprehensive information about a specific KB domain including mastery level, question counts, accuracy history, and recommended practice areas. Accessed from the domain mastery view.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Domain mastery details, question statistics, accuracy history

children.name: KBPractice Launcher
children.description: Pre-session launcher for Knowledge Bowl practice confirming mode, domains, and question count before starting.

ai_enhance.help_text: Final confirmation screen before launching a KB practice session. Summarizes selected mode, domain mix, question count, and time limit. Users confirm or adjust settings before the session begins.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Session launch parameters, mode selection, domain mix, question count

children.name: KBPractice Session
children.description: Generic Knowledge Bowl practice session view used as a base for various training mode presentations.

ai_enhance.help_text: Base practice session view that handles common KB session logic: question display, answer input, scoring, and session completion. Specialized by specific training mode views. Depends on KB scoring algorithms and question bank.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Questions, answers, scoring state, session progress, results

children.name: Audio
children.description: Audio engine managing microphone input, speaker output, audio sessions, and signal processing for voice features.

ai_enhance.help_text: Core audio infrastructure handling AVAudioSession management, microphone recording, speaker playback, and audio format conversion. Provides the audio pipeline that STT and TTS services depend on. Manages audio interruptions and route changes.
ai_enhance.data_handled: Audio buffers, PCM samples, audio session state, microphone/speaker routing

children.name: Config
children.description: App configuration management handling user preferences, API keys, server URLs, and feature flags with persistent storage.

ai_enhance.help_text: Centralized configuration system that manages all app settings including API provider credentials, server connection parameters, feature flags, and user preferences. Persists to UserDefaults and syncs with the management server. Many services depend on this for their configuration.

docs.claude_md:
# KB Audio Test Harness

Component documentation for Claude Code.

## Overview

The KB Audio Test Harness enables iterative testing of the Knowledge Bowl audio Q&A pipeline in the iOS Simulator. It allows you to:

1. Generate TTS audio from expected answers
2. Inject audio directly into STT (bypassing microphone)
3. Get transcript from STT
4. Validate transcript against expected answer semantically
5. Report detailed results with per-phase latencies

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    KBAudioTestHarness (coordinator)                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                          ▼
┌───────────────┐        ┌─────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────┐
│ KBAudioGenerator│       │ KBAudioInjector │        │KBTranscriptValidator│
│ (TTS → Buffer) │        │ (Buffer → STT)  │        │ (Answer Matching)│
└───────────────┘        └─────────────────┘        └─────────────────┘
```

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `KBAudioTestHarness.swift` | Main coordinator actor |
| `KBAudioTestCase.swift` | Test case definition and configuration |
| `KBAudioTestResult.swift` | Result model with detailed metrics |
| `KBAudioGenerator.swift` | TTS audio generation and file loading |
| `KBAudioInjector.swift` | Audio buffer injection into STT |
| `KBTranscriptValidator.swift` | Semantic validation of transcripts |

## Quick Start

```swift
// Create test harness
let harness = KBAudioTestHarness()

// Simple test
let result = try await harness.quickTest(
    question: "What is the capital of France?",
    answer: "Paris"
)

print("Success: \(result.isSuccess)")
print("Transcribed: \(result.transcribedText)")
print("Confidence: \(result.validationResult.confidence)")
```

## Test Case Creation

### Simple Test Case

```swift
let testCase = KBAudioTestCase.simple(
    questionText: "What is the capital of France?",
    expectedAnswer: "Paris",
    answerType: .place
)
```

### From KBQuestion

```swift
let testCase = KBAudioTestCase(
    question: myKBQuestion,
    audioSource: .generateTTS(provider: .appleTTS),
    validationConfig: .standard
)
```

### From Question Set

```swift
let testCases = KBAudioTestCase.fromQuestions(
    myQuestions,
    audioSource: .generateTTS(provider: .appleTTS)
)
```

## Audio Sources

| Source | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.generateTTS(provider:)` | Generate audio via TTS |
| `.prerecordedFile(path:)` | Load from file path |
| `.prerecordedBundle(name:extension:)` | Load from app bundle |
| `.rawAudioData(data:format:)` | Use raw PCM data |

### Supported TTS Providers

For testing, on-device providers are preferred:
- `.appleTTS` - Apple TTS (always available)
- `.kyutaiPocket` - Kyutai Pocket neural TTS

## Validation Configuration

```swift
// Strict: exact/acceptable matches only
let strict = ValidationConfig.strict

// Standard: includes fuzzy matching (default)
let standard = ValidationConfig.standard

// Lenient: includes embeddings and LLM
let lenient = ValidationConfig.lenient

// Custom
let custom = ValidationConfig(
    minimumConfidence: 0.7,
    useFuzzyMatching: true,
    useEmbeddings: true,
    useLLMValidation: false,
    maxPipelineLatencyMs: 5000,
    timeoutSeconds: 30
)
```

## Running Tests

### Single Test

```swift
let result = try await harness.runTest(testCase)
```

### Test Suite

```swift
let suite = KBAudioTestSuite(
    name: "Geography Questions",
    testCases: geographyTestCases,
    repetitions: 3
)

let suiteResult = try await harness.runSuite(suite)
print(suiteResult.summary)
```

### Sample Tests (Debug)

```swift
#if DEBUG
let result = try await harness.runSampleTests()
#endif
```

## Result Analysis

### Single Result

```swift
let result = try await harness.runTest(testCase)

// Success check
if result.isSuccess {
    print("Passed!")
} else {
    print("Failed: \(result.errors)")
}

// Metrics
print("TTS latency: \(result.audioGenerationLatencyMs ?? 0)ms")
print("STT latency: \(result.sttLatencyMs)ms")
print("Validation: \(result.validationLatencyMs)ms")
print("Total: \(result.totalPipelineMs)ms")

// Validation details
print("Match type: \(result.validationResult.matchType)")
print("Confidence: \(result.validationResult.confidence)")
```

### Suite Result

```swift
let suiteResult = try await harness.runSuite(suite)

print("Pass rate: \(suiteResult.passRate * 100)%")
print("Avg pipeline: \(suiteResult.averagePipelineMs)ms")
print("Avg STT latency: \(suiteResult.averageSTTLatencyMs)ms")
print("Avg confidence: \(suiteResult.averageSTTConfidence)")
```

## Custom STT Service

By default, the harness uses on-device Apple Speech. To use a different STT:

```swift
let harness = KBAudioTestHarness(sttService: mySTTService)
// or
await harness.setSTTService(mySTTService)
```

## How It Works

### Audio Generation

1. For TTS sources: Uses `TTSService.synthesize()` to generate audio
2. Collects `TTSAudioChunk` stream into buffer
3. Converts to STT format (16kHz mono float32)

### Audio Injection

1. Chunks buffer into 100ms segments (1600 frames at 16kHz)
2. Starts STT streaming session
3. Sends chunks via `STTService.sendAudio()`
4. Stops streaming and collects final transcript

### Validation

Uses `KBAnswerValidator` with 3-tier validation:
- **Tier 1**: Rule-based (exact, acceptable, fuzzy, phonetic, n-gram)
- **Tier 2**: Embeddings similarity (optional)
- **Tier 3**: LLM judgment (optional)

## Simulator Testing

The harness is designed for Simulator testing:
- Bypasses microphone requirement
- Works without hardware audio
- Enables automated CI testing

## Performance Targets

- TTS generation: <500ms
- STT processing: <2000ms
- Validation: <100ms
- Total pipeline: <3000ms

## Troubleshooting

### No transcript returned

- Check STT service is available
- Verify audio format is correct (16kHz mono float32)
- Try with Apple TTS (most compatible)

### Low confidence scores

- Speech might be unclear (try Apple TTS)
- Expected answer might need alternatives
- Consider using `.lenient` validation

### Test timeouts

- Increase `timeoutSeconds` in ValidationConfig
- Check thermal state (throttling)
- Try simpler test cases first

## Related Files

- `UnaMentis/Services/KnowledgeBowl/KBAnswerValidator.swift` - Validation logic
- `UnaMentis/Testing/LatencyHarness/LatencyTestCoordinator.swift` - Reference pattern
- `UnaMentis/Services/Protocols/STTService.swift` - STT protocol
- `UnaMentis/Services/Protocols/TTSService.swift` - TTS protocol

# UnaMentis iOS App

Swift 6.0/SwiftUI iOS application for voice-first AI tutoring.

## Build Commands

```bash
# Build for simulator (iPhone 16 Pro for CI parity)
xcodebuild -project UnaMentis.xcodeproj -scheme UnaMentis \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16 Pro' build

# Testing - use the unified test runner for CI parity
./scripts/test-quick.sh          # Unit tests only (fast)
./scripts/test-all.sh            # All tests + 80% coverage enforcement
./scripts/test-ci.sh             # Direct runner with env var config

# Run specific test class
xcodebuild test -project UnaMentis.xcodeproj -scheme UnaMentis \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16 Pro' \
  -only-testing:UnaMentisTests/ProgressTrackerTests
```

## MANDATORY: Validate Before Complete

**Use the `/validate` skill before marking any work complete.**

```
/validate           # Lint + quick tests
/validate --full    # Lint + full test suite
```

When adding new files:
1. Verify the file is added to the Xcode project (not just the filesystem)
2. Run `/validate` to confirm compilation and tests pass

See `.claude/skills/validate/SKILL.md` for details.

## Swift 6.0 Strict Concurrency

This codebase uses Swift 6.0 strict concurrency. All code must comply:

### Actors

All services must be actors:

```swift
actor AudioEngine {
    func startRecording() async throws { ... }
}
```

### @MainActor

ViewModels and UI-related code use @MainActor:

```swift
@MainActor
class SessionViewModel: ObservableObject {
    @Published var isRecording = false
}
```

### Sendable

Types crossing actor boundaries must be Sendable:

```swift
struct LLMMessage: Sendable {
    let role: String
    let content: String
}
```

## Architecture

```
UnaMentis/
├── Core/           # Business logic (actors)
│   ├── Audio/      # Audio pipeline, VAD integration
│   ├── Curriculum/ # Curriculum management, progress tracking
│   ├── Session/    # Session management
│   └── Telemetry/  # Metrics, cost tracking
├── Services/       # Provider integrations
│   ├── STT/        # Speech-to-text (AssemblyAI, Deepgram, on-device)
│   ├── TTS/        # Text-to-speech (ElevenLabs, Apple, self-hosted)
│   ├── LLM/        # Language models (OpenAI, Anthropic, local)
│   └── Protocols/  # Service protocol definitions
├── Intents/        # Siri & App Intents (iOS 16+)
├── UI/             # SwiftUI views
└── Persistence/    # Core Data stack
```

## Mandatory Style Requirements

**Read `docs/ios/IOS_STYLE_GUIDE.md` before implementation.** Key requirements:

- Accessibility labels on all interactive elements
- Localizable strings for all user-facing text (use LocalizedStringKey)
- iPad adaptive layouts using size class detection
- Use NavigationStack/NavigationSplitView (not NavigationView)
- Minimum 44x44pt touch targets
- Support Dynamic Type scaling
- Respect Reduce Motion preference

## Service Patterns

All external service integrations follow the protocol pattern:

```swift
protocol STTService: Actor {
    func transcribe(audio: Data) async throws -> TranscriptionResult
}

actor DeepgramSTTService: STTService {
    func transcribe(audio: Data) async throws -> TranscriptionResult { ... }
}
```

## Core Data

Use the persistence controller for all Core Data operations:

```swift
// In production
let controller = PersistenceController.shared

// In tests
let controller = PersistenceController(inMemory: true)
```

## Testing

Tests are in `UnaMentisTests/`. See `AGENTS.md` in the project root for the "Real Over Mock" testing philosophy.

```bash
# From curriculum directory
python -m jsonschema -i examples/knowledge-bowl/science-physics-sample.json spec/umcf-schema.json
```

1. Start with the base UMCF structure
2. Add `extensions.knowledgeBowl` to each content node

# SAT Preparation Curriculum Examples

This directory contains example UMCF curriculum files demonstrating SAT preparation module features.

## Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `math-algebra-sample.json` | Algebra topic with linear equations, systems, and word problems |

## Key Features Demonstrated

### 1. SAT Extensions
- `testVersion`: Digital SAT 2024 format
- `section`: Reading/Writing or Math
- `domain`: Content domain (algebra, geometry, etc.)
- `skill`: Specific College Board skill codes
- `collegeBoardAlignment`: Official skill identifiers

### 2. IRT Difficulty Parameters
```json
"difficultyIRT": {
  "b": 0.5,
  "a": 1.2
}
```
- `b`: Difficulty (-3 to +3, higher = harder)
- `a`: Discrimination (how well it separates ability levels)

### 3. Adaptive Levels
- `module_1`: Calibration questions (critical for routing)
- `module_2_easy`: Lower difficulty second module
- `module_2_hard`: Higher difficulty second module
- `any`: Appropriate for any module

### 4. Error Analysis
Each incorrect answer includes explanation:
```json
"errorAnalysis": {
  "a": "Why students pick this wrong answer",
  "c": "Specific misconception this reveals"
}
```

### 5. Strategy Integration
Questions link to applicable strategies:
```json
"strategyTags": ["substitution", "back_solving", "elimination"]
```

### 6. Timing Targets
Per-question time targets for pacing:
```json
"timeTarget": 75  // seconds
```

## Usage

These examples demonstrate:

1. **Content Structure**: How to organize SAT content hierarchically
2. **Question Formatting**: Proper assessment structure with SAT metadata
3. **Difficulty Calibration**: Using IRT parameters for adaptive practice
4. **Strategy Linking**: Connecting content to test-taking strategies
5. **Error Analysis**: Documenting common mistakes for feedback

## Validation

Validate examples against the schema:

```bash
# From curriculum directory
python -m jsonschema -i examples/sat-prep/math-algebra-sample.json spec/umcf-schema.json
```

## Creating New Content

1. Start with the base UMCF structure
2. Add `extensions.sat` to each content node
3. Include `testVersion` and `section` (required fields)
4. Add IRT parameters for all assessments
5. Include error analysis for each distractor
6. Link applicable strategies

See `/curriculum/spec/SAT_EXTENSIONS.md` for the complete extension specification.

## Score Impact Reference

| Difficulty (b) | Approximate Score Level |
|----------------|------------------------|
| -2.0 to -1.0 | 400-500 |
| -1.0 to 0.0 | 500-550 |
| 0.0 to 0.5 | 550-600 |
| 0.5 to 1.0 | 600-650 |
| 1.0 to 1.5 | 650-700 |
| 1.5+ | 700-800 |

docs.readme:
# Una Mentis Curriculum Format (UMCF)

**A Standards-Based Curriculum Format for Conversational AI Tutoring**

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0--draft-blue.svg)]()
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)]()
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-specification--complete-yellow.svg)]()

---

## Executive Summary

The Una Mentis Curriculum Format (UMCF) is a JSON-based specification for representing educational content optimized for **conversational AI tutoring**. Unlike traditional e-learning formats designed for Learning Management Systems (LMS), UMCF is purpose-built for voice-first, real-time tutoring interactions.

**Key Differentiators:**
- **Voice-native**: Every text field has optional `spokenText` variants optimized for TTS
- **Tutoring-first**: Stopping points, comprehension checks, misconception handling
- **Standards-grounded**: Full traceability to 10+ established educational standards
- **Unlimited hierarchy**: Topics nest to any depth (not limited like SCORM)
- **AI-enrichment ready**: Designed for automated content enhancement

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Vision & Philosophy](#vision--philosophy)
2. [Who This Is For](#who-this-is-for)
3. [What Makes UMCF Different](#what-makes-umcf-different)
4. [Standards Foundation](#standards-foundation)
5. [Specification Overview](#specification-overview)
6. [Import System](#import-system)
7. [AI Enrichment Pipeline](#ai-enrichment-pipeline)
8. [Repository Structure](#repository-structure)
9. [Current Status](#current-status)
10. [Future Direction](#future-direction)
11. [Getting Started](#getting-started)
12. [Contributing](#contributing)

---

## Vision & Philosophy

### The Problem

Existing curriculum standards (SCORM, xAPI, IMSCC) were designed for a different era:
- **LMS-centric**: Optimized for packaging and delivery through course management systems
- **Click-based interaction**: Designed for mouse/keyboard, not voice
- **Static content**: No support for dynamic, conversational tutoring
- **Limited hierarchy**: SCORM caps at ~4 levels of nesting

Modern AI tutors need:
- **Conversational delivery**: Content chunked for turn-by-turn dialogue
- **Comprehension verification**: Natural stopping points for understanding checks
- **Adaptive depth**: Multiple explanation styles for different learners
- **Voice optimization**: Text that sounds natural when spoken

### The Solution: Hub-and-Spoke Architecture

UMCF serves as the **canonical internal format** for tutoring systems, with established standards as import/export "spokes":

```
                    ┌─────────────┐
                    │   SCORM     │
                    │   IMSCC     │
                    │   QTI       │
                    └──────┬──────┘
                           │ Import
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       UMCF                           │
│              (Canonical Format)                      │
│                                                      │
│  • Conversational AI optimized                      │
│  • Voice-first design                               │
│  • Unlimited hierarchy                              │
│  • Rich tutoring metadata                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           │ Tutoring Engine
                           ▼
                ┌─────────────────────┐
                │   UnaMentis App    │
                │   (or any tutor)    │
                └─────────────────────┘
```

### Design Principles

1. **Standards-based, not standards-bound**: Borrow proven patterns, innovate where needed
2. **Voice-native, not voice-adapted**: Designed for speech from the ground up
3. **Tutoring-first, not LMS-first**: Optimized for learning, not administration
4. **AI-ready**: Structured for automated enrichment and generation
5. **Future-proof**: Extension mechanisms for capabilities not yet imagined

---

## Who This Is For

### Primary Audiences

| Audience | Interest |
|----------|----------|
| **Educational Technologists** | Researchers and practitioners building next-generation learning systems |
| **AI/ML Educators** | Those creating AI tutoring systems who need structured content |
| **Curriculum Designers** | Instructional designers wanting voice-first content |
| **EdTech Developers** | Engineers building tutoring platforms |
| **Learning Scientists** | Researchers studying conversational learning |

### Academic Evaluation

This specification was developed with academic rigor and is suitable for evaluation by:
- Educational technology faculty
- Learning science researchers
- Instructional design professionals
- E-learning standards committees

The [Standards Traceability Document](spec/STANDARDS_TRACEABILITY.md) provides field-by-field mappings to established standards for scholarly review.

---

## What Makes UMCF Different

### Comparison with Existing Standards

| Feature | SCORM | xAPI | IMSCC | **UMCF** |
|---------|-------|------|-------|----------|
| **Primary use** | LMS delivery | Activity tracking | Content exchange | **Conversational tutoring** |
| **Content depth** | 3-4 levels | N/A | 2-3 levels | **Unlimited** |
| **Voice support** | None | None | None | **Native** |
| **Stopping points** | None | Verbs only | None | **Rich metadata** |
| **Misconceptions** | None | None | None | **Trigger + remediation** |
| **Alternative explanations** | None | None | None | **Multiple variants** |
| **AI enrichment** | N/A | N/A | N/A | **Purpose-built** |

### Novel Elements in UMCF

These elements are **not borrowed from any standard**—they are innovations for conversational tutoring:

1. **Transcript Segments with Stopping Points**
   ```json
   {
     "segments": [
       {
         "text": "The mitochondria produces ATP through cellular respiration.",
         "spokenText": "The mitochondria produces A T P through cellular respiration.",
         "stoppingPoint": {
           "type": "check_understanding",
           "prompt": "Can you explain what the mitochondria does?",
           "expectedConcepts": ["energy", "ATP", "cell"]
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

2. **Alternative Explanations**
   ```json
   {
     "alternatives": {
       "simpler": "The mitochondria is like a tiny power plant inside each cell.",
       "technical": "Mitochondria are double-membraned organelles that generate ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.",
       "analogy": "Think of mitochondria as the batteries that keep your cells running."
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Misconception Handling**
   ```json
   {
     "misconceptions": [
       {
         "description": "Student thinks mitochondria only exist in animal cells",
         "triggerPhrases": ["only animals", "plants don't have"],
         "remediation": "Actually, both plant and animal cells have mitochondria...",
         "correctUnderstanding": "Mitochondria are found in all eukaryotic cells."
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

4. **Tutoring Configuration**
   ```json
   {
     "tutoringConfig": {
       "depth": "standard",
       "interactionMode": "socratic",
       "scaffoldingLevel": "moderate",
       "checkpointFrequency": "per_concept"
     }
   }
   ```

---

## Standards Foundation

UMCF is built on a foundation of established educational standards:

| Standard | What We Borrow | UMCF Usage |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| **IEEE LOM** (1484.12.1) | Metadata categories, lifecycle | Core metadata structure |
| **LRMI** (Schema.org) | Educational alignment, audience | `educational` block |
| **Dublin Core** | Title, creator, rights, language | Top-level fields |
| **SCORM** | Sequencing, completion tracking | Navigation hints |
| **xAPI** | Activity verbs, extensions | Assessment tracking |
| **CASE** (1EdTech) | Competency framework, objectives | `learningObjectives` |
| **QTI 3.0** | Assessment items, scoring | `assessments` ar

# Curriculum System

This directory contains the Una Mentis Curriculum Format (UMCF) specification and related documentation.

## What is UMCF?

UMCF (Una Mentis Curriculum Format) is a voice-native, conversational AI-optimized curriculum format. It is:

- JSON-based with standards traceability
- Optimized for voice-first learning experiences
- Not SCORM/IMSCC compatible, but inspired by educational standards

# iOS Demo Video Generator

Fully automated pipeline for creating professional iOS app demo videos. Captures from the iOS Simulator, generates voice narration using UnaMentis TTS, and assembles polished videos via Shotstack.

## Features

- **100% Automated**: No manual video editing required
- **UnaMentis TTS**: Uses your own voice AI, not external services
- **Repeatable**: Edit script, regenerate instantly (TTS is cached)
- **Professional Output**: Effects, transitions, 1080p video
- **Cost-Effective**: ~$0.40/minute, free testing with watermark

## Quick Start

### 1. Prerequisites

```bash
# Verify UnaMentis services
/service status
# management-api must be running

# Set Shotstack credentials
export SHOTSTACK_API_KEY="your-key"    # Get at shotstack.io
export SHOTSTACK_ENV="stage"            # Free testing with watermark

# Verify ffmpeg
ffmpeg -version || brew install ffmpeg
```

### 2. Generate Your First Video

```bash
# Run with existing config and script
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/app_overview.json \
  --script demo/scripts/app_overview.md
```

Output: `demo/output/app_overview/UnaMentis_App_Overview.mp4`

## How It Works

```
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐
│   CAPTURE    │───▶│     TTS      │───▶│    UPLOAD    │───▶│   ASSEMBLE   │
│  Simulator   │    │  UnaMentis   │    │   Shotstack  │    │    Video     │
└──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘
```

1. **Capture**: Boot simulator, launch app, navigate via deep links, take screenshots/video
2. **TTS**: Generate voice narration using UnaMentis's own TTS server
3. **Upload**: Push assets to Shotstack's CDN
4. **Assemble**: Build timeline, render video, download result

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `--config <file>` | Config JSON file (required) |
| `--script <file>` | Markdown script for narration |
| `--template` | Print template config |
| `--capture-only` | Only capture, skip video assembly |
| `--skip-capture` | Use existing captures, regenerate video |
| `--skip-preflight` | Skip pre-flight checks |

### Examples

```bash
# Generate template config
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py --template > demo/configs/my_demo.json

# Test capture (no video assembly)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py --config demo/configs/my_demo.json --capture-only

# Regenerate video with updated script (uses cached captures)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/my_demo.json \
  --script demo/scripts/my_demo.md \
  --skip-capture
```

## Configuration

### Config File (JSON)

```json
{
    "name": "My Demo",
    "version": "1.0.0",

    "simulator_device": "iPhone 16 Pro",
    "app_bundle_id": "com.unamentis.app",

    "tts_method": "unamentis",
    "tts_voice": "nova",
    "tts_rate": 175,

    "shotstack_resolution": "1080",
    "background_color": "#0a0a0f",

    "scenes": [
        {
            "id": "welcome",
            "narration": "",
            "capture": "screenshot",
            "wait_before": 2.0,
            "deep_link": null,
            "effect": "zoomIn",
            "transition": "fade"
        }
    ],

    "output_dir": "./demo/output/my_demo"
}
```

### Script File (Markdown)

```markdown
# My Demo Script

## welcome
Welcome to the app. This is the narration for the welcome scene.

## feature_one
Here's the first feature. Narration can span multiple lines.

## closing
Thanks for watching.
```

The `## header` must match the scene `id` in the config.

## TTS Options

| Method | Description | Requirements |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| `unamentis` | UnaMentis TTS server (default) | management-api running |
| `macos` | macOS built-in voices | None |
| `custom` | Your own TTS command | `tts_custom_cmd` in config |
| `prerecorded` | Pre-recorded audio files | `tts_prerecorded_dir` |
| `none` | Video only, no narration | None |

### Available Voices (UnaMentis)
- `nova` (default) - Female, natural
- `sarah` - Female, warm
- `john` - Male, professional
- `emma` - Female, friendly
- `alex` - Male, casual

## Deep Links

Navigate within the app using URL schemes:

| Deep Link | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| `unamentis://chat` | Freeform chat |
| `unamentis://learning` | Learning tab |
| `unamentis://analytics` | Analytics tab |
| `unamentis://settings` | Settings tab |
| `unamentis://history` | History tab |

## Directory Structure

```
demo/
├── configs/           # Demo configurations (JSON)
│   └── app_overview.json
├── scripts/           # Narration scripts (Markdown)
│   └── app_overview.md
├── output/            # Generated files (gitignored)
│   └── app_overview/
│       ├── *.png      # Screenshots
│       ├── *_audio.mp3 # Audio narration
│       └── *.mp4      # Final video
├── tests/             # Test coverage
└── ios_demo_video_generator.py  # Main script
```

## Workflow

### Creating a New Demo

1. **Create config**: Copy template or existing config
2. **Create script**: Write narration in markdown
3. **Test capture**: Run with `--capture-only`, review screenshots
4. **Generate video**: Run full pipeline
5. **Iterate**: Edit script, regenerate with `--skip-capture`

### Editing an Existing Demo

1. **Edit script**: Update `demo/scripts/<name>.md`
2. **Regenerate**: Run with `--skip-capture` (uses cached captures and TTS)

## Cost

|-------------|------|--------|
| `stage` | Free | Watermarked |
| `v1` | ~$0.40/min | Production quality |

Set environment: `export SHOTSTACK_ENV=v1`

## Troubleshooting

### "TTS server not available"
```bash
/service start management-api
```

### "Simulator not found"
```bash
xcrun simctl list devices | grep "iPhone 16 Pro"
```

### "Shotstack API key invalid"
Verify at https://dashboard.shotstack.io

### "ffmpeg not found"
```bash
brew install ffmpeg
```

# Demo Video Generator - Claude Code Instructions

This document provides Claude Code with complete guidance for using and maintaining the iOS demo video automation system.

## Overview

The demo video generator creates professional iOS app demo videos autonomously. It captures screenshots/video from the iOS Simulator, generates voice narration using UnaMentis's own TTS, and assembles everything into a polished video via Shotstack.

**Key Principle**: This system is designed for full autonomy. Once the user approves a script, Claude Code executes the entire pipeline without intervention.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           USER PROVIDES                                  │
│  Direction: "Create a 60-second overview of the voice session feature"  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         CLAUDE CODE DRAFTS                               │
│  Script: demo/scripts/<name>.md (narration text)                        │
│  Config: demo/configs/<name>.json (scenes, timing, effects)             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          USER REVIEWS                                    │
│  Edit script if needed, approve when ready                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CLAUDE CODE EXECUTES PIPELINE                         │
│                                                                          │
│  1. PRE-FLIGHT ──► Verify TTS, Shotstack, Simulator, ffmpeg             │
│  2. CAPTURE ─────► Boot sim, launch app, navigate, capture              │
│  3. TTS ─────────► Generate audio via UnaMentis API (cached)            │
│  4. UPLOAD ──────► Push assets to Shotstack CDN                         │
│  5. ASSEMBLE ────► Build timeline, submit render job                    │
│  6. DOWNLOAD ────► Retrieve final MP4                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                            OUTPUT                                        │
│  demo/output/<name>/<Demo_Name>.mp4                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Directory Structure

```
demo/
├── CLAUDE.md                       # This file - Claude Code instructions
├── README.md                       # Quick start for humans
├── IOS_DEMO_VIDEO_AUTOMATION.md    # Deep technical documentation
├── ios_demo_video_generator.py     # Main generator script (700+ lines)
│
├── configs/                        # Demo configurations (JSON)
│   └── app_overview.json           # Full app walkthrough config
│
├── scripts/                        # Narration scripts (Markdown)
│   └── app_overview.md             # Narration for app overview
│
├── output/                         # Generated files (gitignored)
│   └── <config_name>/              # Output per config
│       ├── *.png                   # Screenshots
│       ├── *.mp4                   # Video clips
│       ├── *_audio.mp3             # Audio narration
│       ├── scenes.json             # Scene metadata (for resume)
│       ├── timeline.json           # Shotstack timeline
│       └── <Demo_Name>.mp4         # Final video
│
└── tests/                          # Test coverage
    ├── __init__.py
    └── test_generator.py           # Unit and integration tests
```

## Prerequisites

Before running the generator, verify:

### 1. UnaMentis Services
```bash
/service status
# management-api must be running for TTS
```

If not running:
```bash
/service start management-api
```

### 2. Shotstack API Key
```bash
# Set in environment
export SHOTSTACK_API_KEY="your-key-here"
export SHOTSTACK_ENV="stage"  # "stage" = free with watermark, "v1" = production
```

Get a key at https://shotstack.io (free tier available, ~$0.40/min for production).

### 3. ffmpeg
```bash
# Install if needed
brew install ffmpeg
```

### 4. iOS Simulator
The config specifies `iPhone 16 Pro` by default. Verify it exists:
```bash
xcrun simctl list devices | grep "iPhone 16 Pro"
```

## Using the Generator

### Command Line Interface

```bash
# Generate template config
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py --template > demo/configs/new_demo.json

# Full pipeline (capture + TTS + assemble)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/app_overview.json \
  --script demo/scripts/app_overview.md

# Capture only (test navigation and screenshots)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/app_overview.json \
  --capture-only

# Assemble only (use existing captures, regenerate video)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/app_overview.json \
  --script demo/scripts/app_overview.md \
  --skip-capture

# Skip pre-flight checks (for debugging)
python demo/ios_demo_video_generator.py \
  --config demo/configs/app_overview.json \
  --skip-preflight
```

### Using the /demo-video Skill

```
/demo-video                         # Show status and available configs
/demo-video generate app_overview   # Full pipeline
/demo-video capture app_overview    # Capture only
/demo-video assemble app_overview   # Assemble only
/demo-video script app_overview     # View narration script
```

# UnaMentis Server API Specification

**Version:** 1.1.0
**Status:** Active
**Last Updated:** 2026-01-25
**Base URL:** `http://localhost:8766` (Management API)

---

## Purpose

This specification documents the UnaMentis server API for client developers. It includes both machine-readable OpenAPI specification and human-readable guides for each API category.

**Target Audience:** AI agents and developers building UnaMentis clients or integrating with the server.

---

## Document Index

| Document | Purpose | Endpoints |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| [openapi.yaml](openapi.yaml) | Machine-readable spec | All endpoints |
| [01-AUTHENTICATION.md](01-AUTHENTICATION.md) | Auth flows | `/api/auth/*` |
| [02-CURRICULA.md](02-CURRICULA.md) | Content management | `/api/curricula/*` |
| [03-SESSIONS.md](03-SESSIONS.md) | Learning sessions | `/api/sessions/*` |
| [04-TTS.md](04-TTS.md) | Voice synthesis | `/api/tts/*` |
| [05-IMPORT.md](05-IMPORT.md) | Content import | `/api/import/*`, `/api/sources/*` |
| [06-MEDIA.md](06-MEDIA.md) | Media generation | `/api/media/*` |
| [07-SYSTEM.md](07-SYSTEM.md) | Health & monitoring | `/api/system/*`, `/health` |
| [08-WEBSOCKET.md](08-WEBSOCKET.md) | Real-time protocols | `/ws` |
| [09-KNOWLEDGE-BOWL.md](09-KNOWLEDGE-BOWL.md) | Knowledge Bowl | `/api/kb/*` |

---

## Quick Reference

### Server Components

| Component | Port | Technology | Purpose |
|-----------|------|------------|---------|
| Management API | 8766 | Python/aiohttp | Content administration, API |
| USM Core | 8787 | Rust/Axum | Cross-platform service management |
| USM (Legacy) | 8767 | Swift | macOS menu bar app (original) |
| Operations Console | 3000 | Next.js/React | System/content management |

### Authentication

All authenticated endpoints require:
```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Token lifecycle:
- Access token: 1 hour validity
- Refresh token: 30 days validity
- Use `/api/auth/refresh` to renew

### Common Response Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200 | Success |
| 201 | Created |
| 400 | Bad Request (validation error) |
| 401 | Unauthorized (invalid/expired token) |
| 403 | Forbidden (insufficient permissions) |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 429 | Rate Limited |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

### Error Response Format

```json
{
  "error": "Human-readable error message",
  "code": "ERROR_CODE",
  "details": {}
}
```

---

## Endpoint Summary

### Authentication (11 endpoints)
- `POST /api/auth/register` - Create account
- `POST /api/auth/login` - Authenticate
- `POST /api/auth/refresh` - Refresh token
- `POST /api/auth/logout` - End session
- `GET /api/auth/me` - Get profile
- `PATCH /api/auth/me` - Update profile
- `POST /api/auth/password` - Change password
- `GET /api/auth/devices` - List devices
- `DELETE /api/auth/devices/{id}` - Remove device
- `GET /api/auth/sessions` - List sessions
- `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` - End session

### Curricula (15+ endpoints)
- `GET /api/curricula` - List curricula
- `POST /api/curricula` - Import curriculum
- `GET /api/curricula/{id}` - Get details
- `GET /api/curricula/{id}/full` - Get complete content
- `DELETE /api/curricula/{id}` - Delete
- `POST /api/curricula/{id}/archive` - Archive
- Visual asset management endpoints
- Topic transcript endpoints

### Sessions/FOV (16 endpoints)
- Session lifecycle (create, start, pause, resume, end)
- Topic and position management
- Conversation turns
- Context building
- Confidence analysis

### TTS (30+ endpoints)
- Basic TTS generation
- Voice profiles
- Pre-generation system
- Cache management
- TTS Lab experimentation (model selection, configuration tuning)

### Import (8 endpoints)
- Source browsing
- Import jobs
- Progress tracking

### Media (7 endpoints)
- Diagram rendering
- Formula rendering
- Map generation

### System (30+ endpoints)
- Health checks
- Metrics
- Service management
- Model management

### WebSocket
- `/ws` - Audio streaming and real-time sync

---

## Related Documentation

- **Client Feature Spec**: [../client-spec/README.md](../client-spec/README.md)
- **Project Overview**: [../architecture/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](../architecture/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md)
- **Voice Lab Guide**: [../server/VOICE_LAB_GUIDE.md](../server/VOICE_LAB_GUIDE.md)
- **TTS Lab Guide**: [../server/TTS_LAB_GUIDE.md](../server/TTS_LAB_GUIDE.md)

---

## Using the OpenAPI Spec

### View with Swagger UI
```bash
npx @redocly/cli preview-docs openapi.yaml
```

### Validate
```bash
npx @redocly/cli lint openapi.yaml
```

### Generate Client SDK
```bash
# TypeScript
npx openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g typescript-fetch -o ./sdk

# Swift
npx openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g swift5 -o ./sdk

# Kotlin
npx openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g kotlin -o ./sdk
```
